title: Variance-scaled influence bound
statement: There is a constant $c>0$ such that, for every natural number $n$ and every function $f:\{0,1\}^n\to\mathbb R$ taking only the values $-1$ and $1$, one has $c\,\operatorname{Var}(f)\,\frac{\log n}{n}\le M(f)$, where variance and coordinate influences are computed under the uniform measure and $M(f)$ is the supremum of the absolute coordinate influences (with the empty supremum interpreted as $0$).
hypotheses_covered: There exists a real constant $c$ with $c>0$
The dimension $n$ is a natural number
$f$ is a real-valued function on the $n$-dimensional Boolean cube
replaced: There exists an absolute $c>0$ such that for every natural dimension $n$ and every $f:\{0,1\}^n\to\{-1,1\}$ under the uniform law, $c\operatorname{Var}(f)(\log n/n)\le\sup_{i\in[n]}|I_i(f)|$, with the empty supremum and division by zero interpreted as zero. For a real cube function $h$, define $I_i(h)=\tfrac14\mathbb E_x(h(x)-h(x^{(i)}))^2$, where $x^{(i)}$ flips coordinate $i$ and $\mathbb E_x$ is uniform expectation.
